chunks.text: Welcome back to the Slow English Podcast.
I'm Emily and today we are traveling to a lovely city in Europe, Yubliana, the capital of Slovenia.
Yubliana is small, green, and peaceful.
It's not very big, but it's full of charm.
Let's explore this friendly European city together.
Part two, where's Ljubljana?
Yubliana is in the center of Europe.
It is the capital city of Slovenia, a small country between Italy, Austria, Hungary, and Croatia.
The city is surrounded by hills and forests.
A beautiful river, the Ljubljanica River flows through the center.
People often walk or ride bicycles by the river.
Part three, a short history of Yubliana.
Yubliana has a long and interesting history.
Long ago, it was part of the Roman Empire.
Later, it became a part of Austria -Hungary, and after that, Yugoslavia.
Today, it is the capital of an independent country, Slovenia.
The old buildings tell stories from the past.
Part four, the city and its streets.
Yubliana city center is very beautiful.
There are colorful houses, small bridges, and many cafes.
The streets are clean and safe.
Many areas are for walking only, no cars.
You can sit by the river and enjoy a cup of coffee while you watch people and boats go by.
Part five, the people of Yubliana.
People in Yubliana are friendly and calm.
They speak Slovene, the national language, but many also speak English very well.
People like to spend time outdoors, walking, cycling, or relaxing in parks.
Family and friends are very important.
Part six, food in Yubliana.
Food in Yubliana is simple but delicious.
One popular dish is zhjonsi, made from cornmeal and served with milk or honey.
People also eat soups, sausages, and fresh bread.
In winter, hot stews are very common.
For dessert, tripodica, a sweet cake with nuts.
It's a favorite in every Slovenian home.
Part seven, markets and daily life.
The main market in Yubliana is next to the river.
It's full of fruits, vegetables, flowers, and local cheese.
People love to buy food directly from farmers.
On weekends, the market is busy and full of life.
You can hear music and smell the fresh bread and coffee.
Part eight, the castle on the hill.
On a hill above the city, there is a big old castle, Yubliana Castle.
You can walk up the hill or take a small train.
From the top, you can see the whole city and the mountains far away.
The castle is a popular place for tourists and local people.
Sometimes there are concerts or art shows inside.
Part nine, art and culture.
Yubliana is a city of art.
There are many museums, galleries, and theaters.
Street art is also very common.
You can see creative paintings on walls all around the city.
One famous place for art and music is Matelkova, a colorful cultural center full of murals and live music.
Part 10, nature and green spaces.
Yubliana is one of the greenest cities in Europe.
There are trees, gardens and parks everywhere.
The biggest park is Tivoli Park, a perfect place for walking, reading, or picnics.
People love to relax there on sunny days.
Even the air feels clean and fresh.
Part 11, festivals and events.
Yubliana has many festivals during the year.
In summer, there are open air concerts, theater shows, and film nights.
People sit by the river, eat ice cream, and listen to music.
In winter, the city has Christmas lights and markets with hot drinks.
The city always feels warm and welcoming.
Part 12, goodbye from Yubliana.
Thank you for joining me on this journey to Yubliana.
It is a city full of peace, culture, and natural beauty.
From its green parks to its calm river, Yubliana shows that small cities can have big hearts.
If you ever visit Europe, remember this charming place.
Goodbye, or as people in Slovenia say, Na svidenje.
